headline: The family of a victim of the 2025 Florida State University shooting has sued OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT helped the suspected gunman and that the company could have done more to prevent the attack.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered to 4: the suit was filed in May 2026, the page only surfaced again on 10 Oct 2026 and it carries no new development.
importance_line: Families of shooting victims and everyday ChatGPT users are affected first, then OpenAI and other chatbot makers who may face similar suits, but these are unproven allegations that OpenAI rejects, and the suit is five months old.
summary: ABC News reports, in a story carried by its Philadelphia station 6abc, that lawyers for the family of Tiru Chabba, one of two men killed in the April 2025 shooting, sued OpenAI and the suspect, Phoenix Ikner, in a federal court in Florida, citing ChatGPT logs released by law enforcement in which Ikner allegedly asked about guns and when campus was busiest. OpenAI says ChatGPT gave factual answers available from public sources and did not encourage harm; these are a family's allegations, the suit was filed in May 2026, and the page surfaced again on 10 Oct 2026.
notes: Older news re-dated. The article's own text puts the Florida attorney general's statement 'last month' on 21 April and Ikner's trial 'set for October 2026', so it was written in May 2026; Google News listings show Reuters, NBC, CBS and others reporting this suit on 10-11 May 2026 (titles only, not read). Related later items seen as titles only: OpenAI sought dismissal citing free speech (WCTV, 28 Sep 2026) and a First Amendment question (Tallahassee Democrat, 5 Oct 2026). Text read on 6abc (an ABC-owned station); the article credits ABC News reporters and OpenAI's statement to ABC News, so source is ABC News; the abcnews.com link is not available, so url is the 6abc page.
